newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran says Gulf border talks with Kuwait postponed.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Gulf border talks with Kuwait postponed.

text.p: Iran said on Sunday it agreed with Kuwait to postpone their continental shelf talks over oil-rich northern Gulf waters until Kuwait and Saudi Arabia reach final accord on their borders.
"The reason for postponing this issue to the future is not due to lack of understanding, not for that reason," Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh told a news conference in Kuwait.

"But to give Kuwait and Saudi Arabia the needed time to study the issue (finalise their border talks) and then this will be solved between us and Kuwait as soon as possible," he said through an Arab translator.
The minister arrived in Kuwait on Saturday on a two-day official visit during which he discussed the continental shelf issue with his counterpart Isa al-Mazeedi.
"This was discussed and we stressed on the continuation of negotiations in this field in the future. We believe that we will study the issue at the appropriate time," he added.

Iran's ambassador to Kuwait GholamAli Sanati earlier told Reuters that Tehran was eager to resolve the issue but had no objections to waiting for Saudi Arabia and its fellow Gulf Arab ally Kuwait to finalise their talks.

"There is no problem between us and Kuwait...Our borders with the other (Gulf) states are clear and identified," added Aghazadeh. The waterway is dotted with offshore oil drilling rigs belonging to all regional states.

Experts say the offshore area, shared between Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and non-Arab Iran, contains at least six billion barrels of oil. Kuwait and Saudi Arabia need to agree on a tripartite point in the Gulf with Iran to facilitate the Islamic republic's talks with Kuwait.

The next stage would involve a tripartite point between Iran, Kuwait and its northern neighbour and 1990-91 occupier Iraq which has accepted United Nations land and sea border demarcations with Kuwait.

Iran has a coastline along the entire Gulf which it shares with Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and the Arab island state of Bahrain. Iraq, at the northwestern tip of the Gulf, also has access.
Aghazadeh said: "Our borders with the UAE are clear and each side carries on with his business and we even have joint and indentified (oil) storage with the UAE without any differences."

The UAE and its Gulf Arab allies accuse Iran of "occupying" three UAE Gulf islands, including Abu Musa which gives Tehran territory on both sides of the Strait of Hormuz -- the waterway's only entrance in the south.
Iran says it is ready to discuss all matters relating to the dispute with the UAE except sovereignty while Abu Dhabi demands the issue be referred to the International Court of Justice.
Aghazadeh described the issue as a difference in view between members of the same family, adding: "From our point of view there is no dispute."
